name: Evidence Action's Equal Vitamin Access, India (The Life You Can Save, 2025)
beneficiaries_note: The model's name: Evidence Action's Equal Vitamin Access, India (The Life You Can Save, 2025).

missing_data.note: Partly thin (50%): Evidence Action counts the tablets given through the states' records, but the children it credits as reached because of its support are its own estimate against a 2020-21 baseline; the fall in anaemia is from trials of weekly iron and folic acid.

summary: Evidence Action helps Indian states give school-aged children and adolescents weekly iron and folic acid tablets to prevent anaemia. The Life You Can Save counts the anaemia cases and deaths Evidence Action estimates it averted in 2024 among the 4.7 million extra children it credits to its support, and divides by its 2024 cost. Our view values the deaths the site's way and adds the later gains of less anaemia; the biggest uncertainties are how many children are reached because of Evidence Action and what less anaemia is worth beyond health.

resources.title: The Life You Can Save, cost-effectiveness analysis spreadsheet for Evidence Action
resources.note: Three tabs, one per programme; this model is the 'EVA' tab (India, 2024). Every calculated row of this model reproduces its cell.

sections.title: Anaemia cases by severity
sections.explainer: The Life You Can Save splits the cases averted in the proportions of mild, moderate and severe anaemia among Indian children: under-fives from the 2019-21 Demographic and Health Survey, and 10-19-year-olds' total prevalence spread in the same proportions.

sections.title: Deaths valued the site's way
sections.explainer: charityevals' step: the babies' deaths averted are valued like every newborn's death on the site; the anaemia averted keeps the sheet's DALYs; the later gains of less anaemia are a side effect.

sections.title: Costs the sheet leaves out
sections.explainer: charityevals' step: Evidence Action's central costs, and with credit by share of resources on, its staff's pay below market and the states' cost of the extra tablets.

rows.label: Value of averting a newborn's death, in healthy years
rows.explainer: **Changed for consistency.** The sheet counts each death at the remaining life expectancy at age 2.5, discounted (29.2 years). These deaths are of babies with neural tube defects, around birth; the site values them like every newborn's death: GiveWell's weight for a neonatal death times the value-of-a-life slider, in healthy years at Your values' exchange rate.

rows.label: Share of the children's tablets that wouldn't have been given without Evidence Action
rows.explainer: ×1, our judgment: Evidence Action already counts only the children reached beyond the states' coverage before its support. Whether that estimate is right is the missing-data step's question.

rows.label: Later gains of less anaemia (learning, earnings), as a share of the health years
rows.explainer: Anaemia in school-aged children lowers attention and learning; GiveWell's models of iron supplementation put most of their value in later earnings. The sheet counts only health. Our judgment, 50% (0 to 150%) of the health years.

rows.label: Our healthy years for the same work, as a share of The Life You Can Save's DALYs
rows.explainer: The evaluator view keeps The Life You Can Save's (1).

rows.label: Evidence Action's spending beyond the programme's cost, per dollar of it
rows.explainer: The programme cost is what was billed to it; Evidence Action's headquarters, management and fundraising come on top. Our judgment, 10% (0 to 20%).

rows.label: States' cost per extra child given tablets for a year
rows.explainer: The states buy and distribute the tablets; the sheet takes their extra cost as zero because their budgets didn't rise against 2020-21. With credit by share of resources on, their money spent on the extra children shares the outcome. Our judgment of the tablets and teachers' time per child-year.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of programme cost
rows.explainer: Default for technical assistance: Evidence Action's staff advise and monitor the states' programmes. Our judgment.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Advisers and policy staff. Our judgment.
